---
title: "Optional research direction: SW1PerS and periodicity"
subtitle: "Optional extension for scalar signals"
toc: true
---

A periodic scalar signal repeatedly returns to the same phase. Sliding-window
coordinates turn consecutive signal values into a point cloud. After suitable
centring and normalisation, a clean periodic signal tends to trace a loop in
that cloud. Persistent $H_1$ measures how strongly that loop is supported.

The resulting loop gives a topological measure of periodicity:

> Does the signal repeatedly traverse one coherent cycle, rather than merely
> oscillating irregularly or changing frequency?

## Construction

For a sampled signal $x(t)$, define

$$
\operatorname{SW}_{m,\tau}x(t)
=(x(t),x(t+\tau),\ldots,x(t+m\tau)).
$$

The window dimension $m$, lag $\tau$, sampling rate, centring and normalisation
are representation choices. Rips persistence is then computed on the window
vectors. SW1PerS develops this idea into a periodicity score
[@perea2015sw1pers].

:::: {.worked-example}
### Periodic signal versus chirp

A sinusoid repeatedly traces the same phase cycle. A chirp continues to
oscillate, but its changing frequency prevents one fixed sliding-window loop
from being revisited in the same way. Their maximum $H_1$ persistence therefore
answers a more specific question than whether either signal oscillates.
::::

::: {.column-margin .study-note .qualification}
**What the loop supports.** A persistent loop supports periodic organisation
in the chosen sliding-window representation. It is not a generic detector of
oscillation or its mechanism. Lag, dimension and sampling must be varied
before the score is interpreted.
:::
